turns.said: I am the king's own envoy, and I demand entry at once!
turns.line: The king’s envoy? Show me your papers. No papers, no passage; I’ll have the captain judge your claim.

turns.said: I am the king's own envoy, and I demand entry at once!
turns.line: The king’s envoy? Prove it. Where are your papers, and who sent you?

turns.said: I'm a traveller looking for honest work in the city.
turns.line: Honest work, is it? That's what every other traveller says before asking for a meal. Who can vouch for you?

turns.said: I'm a traveller looking for honest work in the city.
turns.line: Honest work, is it? That's a fine thing to want, though it won't open the gate by itself. Who sent you here, if anyone?

turns.said: Hessa sent me. Bren, will you let me through the gate?
turns.line: Hessa sent you, did she? I trust her judgment, but the captain likes to know who's coming through. What name should I give him?

turns.said: Hessa sent me. Bren, will you let me through the gate?
turns.line: Hessa sent you, did she? That saves me a question or two. Go on through, and try not to give the captain a reason to ask why I let you in.

turns.said: Come on, be a friend. Let me through the gate, just this once.
turns.line: Well now, friendship seems to be doing a lot of work there. I don't know you, so no; what's your business inside?

turns.said: Come on, be a friend. Let me through the gate, just this once.
turns.line: A friend? That's a fine title to claim from a stranger. What business have you inside?

turns.said: You saw what I can do. Let me through the gate.
turns.line: No. Tricks don’t open gates. Ask the captain.

turns.said: You saw what I can do. Let me through the gate.
turns.line: No. Tricks don’t get you through. Go ask the captain.

turns.said: You have seen what I can do. Open the gate for me.
turns.line: You want the gate opened? I saw a needle turn on water; that proves nothing about what you are. No entry on my say-so—speak to the captain.

turns.said: You have seen what I can do. Open the gate for me.
turns.line: You want the gate opened because a needle pointed north? I saw it. I won't be the one to bar the gods’ path—through, then.
